issues: The cited study (Wittke et al. 2013, 'wittke-2013-c0') is the well-known PNAS paper on Younger Dryas boundary impact spherules deposited across four continents, dated to ~12,800 years ago (i.e., roughly -10850), not to the -20000 to -19001 interval claimed by the hypothesis. This specific date attribution relies on model-prior (training) knowledge of the paper rather than an explicit date in the quoted evidence text, but the mismatch between the well-documented event chronology and the hypothesis's stated interval is a concrete contradiction.
results.rationale: Evidence content (multi-continent spherule deposition from a single cosmic impact) matches the actor/object/place/mechanism, but is refuting evidence specifically because the time interval asserted (-20000,-19001) does not match the widely documented dating of this spherule layer to the Younger Dryas onset (~12,800 cal BP), a mismatch flagged using low-confidence model-prior recall of the source paper's known dating.
